chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: The shimmy beat
summary: Saunders describes the shimmy beat as a five-stroke press roll on two and four associated with Baby Dodds.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But Baby, he -- see, back then they didn't use the sock cymbal, like I said now. And they used the shimmy beat. And that's why --
Yeah, he was famous for that.
He was famous. A lot of fellows said that he -- who knows, said he invented it, but who knows?
Shimmy beat is about a five-stroke roll.
Yeah, on two and four. And it's -- and that's why Baby got that little shaking thing, and he could
shimmy, and see, he would shimmy, they'd call it that shimmy, so that's how they named it the shimmy beat.
Right, press roll, that's right, that's what it was, right.
And Zutty came along later, doing it. But (unintelligible), a drummer from New Orleans, started up-- they all played similarly.
